transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-23
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood CSM briefly), Alex (Hightide Head of Search), Priya (ML Eng), Noah (Platform), Sara (Privacy)

Summary:
Hightide is evaluating Redwood for embeddings + reranking for their site search and personalized recommendations. Primary concerns: vector DB integration (they currently run Milvus in prod, evaluating Weaviate), throughput (target 200-500 QPS at peak), embedding dimensionality (1536 vs 768 tradeoffs), hybrid search (BM25 + embeddings rerank), latency/cost tradeoffs, and private deployment/networking for EU data residency. They asked about hosted vs dedicated vs private (on-prem/VPC) options, SOC2/KMS support, and a short benchmark to validate P95 latency and cost. Next steps and owners agreed.

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll kick off - I'm Jordan, AE on the account, with Maya our SE. Quick intros?
00:07 Alex (Hightide): Hi, Alex here, Hightide, head of search. Priya and Noah are with me, and Sara from privacy will pop in later.
00:12 Maya (Redwood-SE): Hi all, Maya - I'll mostly handle the technical Qs. Quick agenda: understand current infra, key metrics, and map to Redwood Hosted / Dedicated / Private options.
00:22 Priya (Hightide): Great. Quick background: we run a site search + product recommendation stack. Currently elastic for indexing and Milvus for vector store. We embed with open model 1536-d vectors, roughly 1.2M documents right now. Peak QPS ~350 for read/search, avg 120 QPS.
00:38 Jordan: Nice, thanks. So you're doing hybrid? Elastic BM25 then embeddings rerank?
00:42 Priya: Yeah, BM25 for candidate retrieval then embedding rerank. Looking to reduce latency and cost - Milvus cluster is kinda heavy and ops cost is high. Also thinking about moving to a hosted vector DB or a unified inference+vector solution.
00:58 Maya: Understood. A few qualification q's: what's your P95 latency SLO for search? And do you need real-time ingestion or can you batch?
01:05 Alex: P95 target is 200ms end-to-end for the reranked results, ideally under 150ms if possible. Ingestion is near-real-time, we push updates every 30s to 2 min. We can't tolerate long KV cache warm-ups.
01:18 Maya: OK. For 1536-d vectors, throughput and cost are both sensitive to quantization and kernel choices. Redwood Hosted can serve open models and embeddings, Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput, and Private is for VPC/on-prem for data residency. For reranking at 350 QPS peak, we'd probably recommend Dedicated or a hybrid: Hosted for model generation, Dedicated for heavy QPS serving, or a Private deployment if EU-only data.
01:40 Noah (Hightide): Quick Q: how do you integrate with external vector DBs like Milvus or Weaviate? We have lots of client-side tooling that expects Milvus APIs.
01:48 Maya: We have connector patterns. Two options: 1) Redwood handles embeddings and serves the k-NN search in our runtime (we do ANN and can act as the vector backend), or 2) Redwood generates embeddings and pushes them to your Milvus/Weaviate; queries can either go through us for reranking or you can perform ANN in your vector DB and call us for reranking only. Option 1 reduces network hops and can lower end-to-end latency. Option 2 keeps your current operational surface.
02:12 Priya: That first option sounds appealing but ops will push back if we lose control of the vector store.
02:17 Sara (Hightide): Also, for data residency, any hosted path must ensure EU data stays in-region or go Private. We need SOC2 and KMS support for keys.
02:25 Jordan: Absolutely. We have hosted regions in EU, SOC2 Type II, and KMS/HSM integrations for Dedicated and Private. For Private you control the KMS keys entirely.
02:33 Alex: On accuracy - we currently use 1536-d embeddings from model X, wondering if switching to 768-d would save cost with minimal perf loss. Any experience?
02:41 Maya: Generally, lower dims reduce index size and compute and improve throughput. Tradeoff: recall/precision can drop, but quantization (like int8/4) and model distillation sometimes mitigate that. We usually run a small eval on a held-out query set (1000 queries) comparing 1536 vs 768 and also try OPQ/IVF configs in the ANN index. We'll share a recommended matrix.
03:03 Alex: Nice. For the ANN algorithm do you recommend HNSW vs IVF+PQ?
03:08 Maya: HNSW tends to give stable recall and low latency, especially for dynamic indexes with frequent updates. IVF+PQ is better for large static corpora when memory is constrained. For your 1.2M vectors and real-time ingestion, HNSW is usually simpler operationally. But if you need smaller memory footprint, IVF+PQ with optimized PQ dim works too.
03:26 Priya: How about similarity metric - cosine vs dot product?
03:29 Maya: Cosine is common for normalized embeddings; dot product is fine if you want inner-product scoring. Our runtime supports both; if you're using BM25 + embeddings hybrid, we normalize scores in the reranker.
03:39 Noah: Latency numbers - can you give bucketed latency for a 1536-d HNSW rerank at 300 QPS on dedicated vs hosted? I know it's fuzzy.
03:47 Maya: Rough estimate: on Dedicated with reserved GPUs and optimized kernels, P95 ~120-180ms end-to-end (embedding generation + ANN + rerank) for 300 QPS if you enable batching and a small prefix KV cache. Hosted may be slightly higher P95 - 160-240ms depending on contention and region. Private on-prem could be in range but depends on networking and instance types. We'll run an actual benchmark to be precise.
04:12 Alex: Cost conversation - what's per-query cost ballpark? We want <$0.0005 per query at scale.
04:18 Jordan: Cost depends on mode. Hosted variable, Dedicated reserved capacity lowers unit cost. With intelligent batching, prefix caching, and offloading ANN to a vector DB you can reduce per-query compute. We'll include cost scenarios in the pricing doc.
04:30 Priya: For our use case we might offload ANN to Milvus and call Redwood for reranking only. Concern: extra network hop adds 20-40ms. Can Redwood colocate or provide a connector to reduce that?
04:41 Maya: We can colocate Dedicated nodes in same VPC or region, or in Private you can run our runtime inside your VPC to avoid cross-network. Also we have asynchronous prefetching and KV caching to reduce repeated ANN calls.
04:55 Noah: Security checklist - SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, SOC2, encryption at rest, KMS, customer-managed keys?
05:02 Jordan: All supported. Hosted: SOC2, region controls, SSE, and customer KMS for encryption at rest; Dedicated: we offer customer-managed KMS and extended audit logs; Private: full KMS control, HSM options. We'll attach security whitepaper and SOC2 cert.
05:17 Sara: For Private deployment, network egress and ingress rules are critical. We need documentation for required ports, IP ranges, and whether agents push or pull for ingestion.
05:26 Maya: We'll provide a networking diagram and template firewall rules; agents can be either push or pull, but push is common for low-latency ingestion.
05:33 Alex: Anything else on model choices? We're also experimenting with low-dim distilled models and post-processing rerankers.
05:39 Maya: We support custom models for embeddings; you can bring your own model and we can serve it in our runtime (Hosted/Dedicated/Private). For quantization, we recommend 8-bit or 4-bit for embeddings if accuracy holds. We'll include quant profiles for 1536/768 dims.
05:55 Priya: About indexing - we want near-real-time updates every minute. How fast can you make newly ingested docs searchable?
06:01 Maya: With HNSW and our incremental index pipeline, sub-30s visibility is doable with Dedicated or Private. Hosted might have a slightly longer tail depending on config. We'll show benchmark data.
06:12 Alex: Ok, last thing - any reference customers in fintech or EU-regulated sectors?
06:17 Jordan: Yes, we have a fintech customer using Dedicated with VPC peering in EU, happy to share a reference once NDA is in place.
06:24 Alex: Great. That covers most of it.
06:27 Jordan: Cool. Quick recap - we'll send pricing for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, benchmark plan for 1M vectors and 48h run, security docs, and schedule the deep-dive on VPC/KMS. Any other blockers?
06:40 Priya: No, just that we want to make sure the benchmark includes both full rerank path and variant where Milvus does ANN and Redwood only reranks.
06:49 Maya: Noted. We'll run both.
06:52 Alex: Thanks everyone. We'll aim to share sample data and internal QPS schedule by Friday.
06:57 Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with next steps.

End of transcript.
